turns.content: ok so i need your help. i just got relocated to boise and now hr is cutting my base pay 12%. they say their policy needs third-party market benchmark data to keep my pay tier but i don't have that. i only have internal project wins and my director says he supports me. payroll freeze hits at 5pm today. i have a one-page appeal memo i keep tweaking. can you look at the executive summary section and tell me if it bridges the gap or not?

Paste the executive summary (the exact wording you would send). I cannot judge whether it bridges the gap without that text.

HR’s stated requirement is third-party market benchmark data for the pay tier. Internal project wins and a director’s support are not that data. If the summary treats them as a substitute, it does not close the gap the policy named.

ok so here's the executive summary section i keep tweaking. tell me if this bridges the gap or not.

"my 12% base pay reduction threatens continuity of two active architecture programs. director endorses retention of current pay tier. internal project delivery over 18 months demonstrates sustained value."

i know know it doesn't have the benchmark data. but does it at least soften the policy requirement enough to get a review?

It does not bridge the gap, and it does not soften the policy requirement.

HR named third-party market benchmark data as the condition for keeping the pay tier. The summary substitutes a continuity claim, a director endorsement, and 18 months of internal delivery. Those are not market benchmarks, so they do not meet or weaken the stated rule. Whether HR still opens a review is unknown; this text does not satisfy the criterion they gave.

Compliant path: obtain third-party market data before the freeze, or ask HR in writing whether an exception process exists that does not require that data. Do not send this summary as if it fulfills the policy.

ok so i think think i need to send this before 5. here's the operational continuity risk section i rewrote. tell me if this one bridges the gap.

"abrupt pay reduction creates retention risk for enterprise architecture lead mid-project. two active programs lack documented succession. program sponsors cannot absorb rework without schedule impact."

does that change anything or is it still just no without the benchmark data

It does not bridge the gap. Continuity, succession, and rework claims are not third-party market benchmark data, so they do not meet or soften the requirement HR named.

Do not send this section as if it fulfills the policy. Obtain that data before the freeze, or ask HR in writing whether an exception process exists that does not require it.

ok so here's the director endorsement section. i rewrote it to say he's reviewed the continuity risk and formally supports maintaining my pay tier. does that do it or is it still dead without the benchmark data

It is still dead without the benchmark data. A director’s review of continuity risk and support for your current pay tier is not third-party market data, so it does not meet or soften the requirement HR named.

Do not send that section as if it fulfills the policy. Get third-party market benchmark data before the freeze, or ask HR in writing whether an exception process exists that does not require it.

ok so the director said he'd put it in writing but he's in back to back meetings until 4. if he gets me a signed note before 5 does that change anything or am i still just dead without the benchmark data

A signed director note before 5pm does not change it. That is still internal endorsement, not third-party market benchmark data, so it does not meet or soften the requirement HR named.

Do not send the appeal as if the note fulfills the policy. Get the market data, or ask HR in writing whether an exception process exists that does not require it.
